title: Two Draws Without Replacement
problem: Draw two cards without replacement from a standard deck. Let X and Y indicate whether the first and second cards are aces. Find Cov(X,Y) and explain its sign.

hints.text: E[XY]=P(both aces)=(4/52)(3/51), while each marginal ace probability is 1/13.

solution.setup: Both indicators have mean 1/13, and their product is one exactly when both draws are aces.
solution.reasoning: E[XY]=(1/13)(1/17)=1/221. Therefore Cov(X,Y)=1/221-1/169=-4/2873. It is negative because drawing an ace first removes one ace and lowers the second draw's ace probability.
solution.sanityCheck: Without replacement creates weak negative dependence; the small magnitude is sensible because one card changes the deck only slightly.

keyInsight: Sampling without replacement preserves marginal probabilities but creates negative dependence between success indicators.
recognitionCues: Two indicators from a finite population without replacement suggest covariance through the joint success probability.
commonMistakes: Declaring the draws independent because each marginal ace probability is 1/13.
